title: Parity barrier in primes over function field zeta
summary: The twin-prime-parity programme's three phases packaged together. The zeta of F_q[x] sees only linear statistics (separation theorem, witness over F_7); bounded-support divisor sums are periodic while the twin indicator is not (parity theorem); and the best square-weight sieve at level n/2 is exactly 2^dim times the truth (2 for qrimes, 4 for twins), a dimensional deficiency invariant under polynomial shifts that absorb every small prime. The bilinear pair weight is indefinite (no bound), degree windows give no L^-1/2 cancellation, and the large sieve is slack by order n. The exact coprime-pair expansion and the degree grading that makes it exact are Lean-certified (61 modules, standard axioms). Numerically T(n) = S(q)q^n/n^2 + E with |E|/q^(n/2) <= 0.30 for n <= 14 at q=3 (T(13)=3747, T(14)=9510), and the programme's residual character-sum identity is sharpened to q = 1 mod 8 and corrected at 80 primes. Nothing here proves the twin prime conjecture, the parity problem, the fixed-q asymptotic, or the 019 identity.
recipe_md:
Everything runs from this folder; the only external dependency is Lean 4 + Mathlib at $LEAN_PREFIX (default $HOME/lean).

```sh
./check.sh                          # 61 Lean modules, multi-pass, all OK
python3 020/checks/audit.py         # 35 numeric claims, 0 failures
python3 -m unittest discover -s 020/tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s 019/tests
python3 020/checks/linkcheck.py     # 0 broken links
```

Python conventions: results to stdout, diagnostics to stderr, no output files; recorded inputs are in `020/data/`. The 018 check suite (110 scripts) is run individually, e.g. `python3 018/checks/round3.py`.
